{{Short description|Triangle geometry term}}
In [[geometry]] the '''Gossard perspector'''<ref name=Clark>{{cite web|last=Kimberling |first=Clark |title=Gossard Perspector |url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/tcenters/recent/gosspersp.html |access-date=17 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120510142023/http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/tcenters/recent/gosspersp.html |archive-date=10 May 2012 }}</ref> (also called the '''Zeeman–Gossard perspector'''<ref name=ETC>{{cite encyclopedia|last=Kimberling |first=Clark |title=X(402) = Zeemann--Gossard perspector |url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html#X402 |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers |access-date=17 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419171900/http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html |archive-date=19 April 2012 }}</ref>) is a special point associated with a [[Plane (geometry)|plane]] [[triangle]].  It is a [[triangle center]] and it is designated as X(402) in [[Clark Kimberling]]'s [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]]. The point was named ''Gossard perspector'' by [[John Horton Conway|John Conway]] in 1998 in honour of   [[Harry Clinton Gossard]] who discovered its existence in 1916. Later it was learned
that the point had appeared in an article by [[Christopher Zeeman]] published during 1899 – 1902. From 2003 onwards the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers has been referring to this point as ''Zeeman–Gossard perspector''.<ref name=ETC/>

==Definition==
[[File:Gossard perspector.svg|thumb|400px|''H'', ''H<sub>A</sub>'', ''H<sub>B</sub>'', ''H<sub>C</sub>'', ''H<sub>g</sub>'' are [[orthocenter]]s, and ''G'', ''G<sub>A</sub>'', ''G<sub>B</sub>'', ''G<sub>C</sub>'', ''G<sub>g</sub>'' are centroids of triangles ''ABC'', ''AEF'', ''BFD'', ''CDE'', ''A<sub>g</sub>B<sub>g</sub>C<sub>g</sub>'' respectively.]]

===Gossard triangle===

Let ''ABC'' be any triangle. Let the [[Euler line]] of triangle ''ABC'' meet the sidelines ''BC'', ''CA'' and ''AB'' of triangle ''ABC'' at ''D'', ''E'' and ''F'' respectively. Let ''A<sub>g</sub>B<sub>g</sub>C<sub>g</sub>'' be the triangle formed by the Euler lines of the triangles ''AEF'', ''BFD'' and ''CDE'', the vertex ''A<sub>g</sub>'' being the intersection of the Euler lines of the triangles ''BFD'' and ''CDE'', and similarly for the other two vertices. 
The triangle ''A<sub>g</sub>B<sub>g</sub>C<sub>g</sub>'' is called the '''Gossard triangle''' of triangle ''ABC''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kimberling |first=Clark |title=Harry Clinton Gossard |url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/bstud/gossard.html |access-date=17 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130522042839/http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/bstud/gossard.html |archive-date=22 May 2013 }}</ref>

===Gossard perspector===

Let ''ABC'' be any triangle and let ''A<sub>g</sub>B<sub>g</sub>C<sub>g</sub>'' be its Gossard triangle.  Then the lines ''AA<sub>g</sub>'', ''BB<sub>g</sub>'' and ''CC<sub>g</sub>'' are concurrent. The point of concurrence is called the ''Gossard perspector'' of triangle ''ABC''.

==Properties==
*Let ''A<sub>g</sub>B<sub>g</sub>C<sub>g</sub>'' be the Gossard triangle of triangle ''ABC''. The lines ''B<sub>g</sub>C<sub>g</sub>'', ''C<sub>g</sub>A<sub>g</sub>'' and ''A<sub>g</sub>B<sub>g</sub>'' are respectively parallel to the lines ''BC'', ''CA'' and ''AB''.<ref name=Antreas>{{cite web|last=Hatzipolakis|first=Antreas P.|title=Hyacinthos Message #7564|url=http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/Hyacinthos/message/7564|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130105143601/http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/Hyacinthos/message/7564|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 5, 2013|access-date=17 June 2012}}</ref> 
*Any triangle and its Gossard triangle are congruent.
*Any triangle and its Gossard triangle have the same Euler line.
*The Gossard triangle of triangle ''ABC'' is the reflection of triangle ''ABC'' in the Gossard perspector.

===Trilinear coordinates===

The [[trilinear coordinates]] of the Gossard perspector of triangle ''ABC'' are
: ( ''f'' ( ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' ) : ''f'' ( ''b'', ''c'', ''a'' ) : ''f'' ( ''c'', ''a'', ''b'' ) )
where
: ''f'' ( ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' ) = ''p'' ( ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' ) ''y'' ( ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' ) / ''a'' 
where
: ''p'' ( ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' ) = 2''a''<sup>4</sup> &minus; ''a''<sup>2</sup>''b''<sup>2</sup> &minus; ''a''<sup>2</sup>''c''<sup>2</sup> &minus; ( ''b''<sup>2</sup> &minus; ''c''<sup>2</sup> )<sup>2</sup>
and
: ''y'' ( ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' ) = ''a''<sup>8</sup> &minus; ''a''<sup>6</sup> ( ''b''<sup>2</sup> + ''c''<sup>2</sup> ) + ''a''<sup>4</sup> ( 2''b''<sup>2</sup> &minus; ''c''<sup>2</sup> ) ( 2''c''<sup>2</sup> &minus; ''b''<sup>2</sup> ) + ( ''b''<sup>2</sup> &minus; ''c''<sup>2</sup> )<sup>2</sup> [ 3''a''<sup>2</sup> ( ''b''<sup>2</sup> + ''c''<sup>2</sup> ) &minus; ''b''<sup>4</sup> &minus; ''c''<sup>4</sup> &minus; 3''b''<sup>2</sup>''c''<sup>2</sup> ]
[[File:Gossard perspector generalisation.gif|thumb|400px|In the figure, ''DEF'' is the Euler line of triangle ''ABC''. The line ''XYZ'' moves parallel to the line ''DEF''. The triangle ''A'B'C'&nbsp;'' remains congruent to triangle ''ABC'' whatever be the position of the line ''XYZ''. The blue 'inverted' triangle is the Gossard triangle of triangle ''ABC''.]]

==Generalizations==
The construction yielding the Gossard triangle of a triangle ''ABC'' can be generalised to produce triangles ''A'B'C'&nbsp;'' which are [[Congruence (geometry)|congruent]] to triangle ''ABC'' and whose sidelines are [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to the sidelines of triangle ''ABC''.

===Zeeman’s Generalization ===

This result is due to Christopher Zeeman.<ref name=Antreas/>

Let ''l'' be any line parallel to the [[Euler line]] of triangle ''ABC''. Let ''l'' intersect the sidelines ''BC'', ''CA'', ''AB'' of triangle ''ABC'' at ''X'', ''Y'', ''Z'' respectively. Let ''A'B'C'&nbsp;'' be the triangle formed by the Euler lines of the triangles ''AYZ'', ''BZX'' and ''CXY''. Then triangle ''A'B'C'&nbsp;'' is congruent to triangle ''ABC'' and its sidelines are parallel to the sidelines of triangle ''ABC''.<ref name=Antreas/>

===Yiu’s Generalization ===
[[File:Gossard perspector generalisation02.svg|thumb|400px|Paul Yiu's generalisation of Gossard triangle.]]
This generalisation is due to [[Paul Yiu]].<ref name=Clark/><ref>{{cite web|last=Grinberg|first=Darij|title=Hyacithos Message #9666|url=http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/Hyacinthos/message/9666|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130105223625/http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/Hyacinthos/message/9666|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 5, 2013|access-date=18 June 2012}}</ref>

Let ''P'' be any point in the plane of the [[triangle]] ''ABC'' different from its [[centroid]] ''G''.
:Let the line ''PG'' meet the sidelines ''BC'', ''CA'' and ''AB'' at ''X'', ''Y'' and ''Z'' respectively. 
:Let the centroids of the triangles ''AYZ'', ''BZX'' and ''CXY'' be ''G<sub>a</sub>'', ''G<sub>b</sub>'' and ''G<sub>c</sub>'' respectively.
:Let ''P<sub>a</sub>'' be a point such that ''YP<sub>a</sub>'' is [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''CP'' and ''ZP<sub>a</sub>'' is [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''BP''.
:Let ''P<sub>b</sub>'' be a point such that ''ZP<sub>b</sub>'' is [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''AP'' and ''XP<sub>b</sub>'' is [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''CP''.
:Let ''P<sub>c</sub>'' be a point such that ''XP<sub>c</sub>'' is [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''BP'' and ''YP<sub>c</sub>'' is [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''AP''.
:Let ''A'B'C'&nbsp;'' be the triangle formed by the lines ''G<sub>a</sub>P<sub>a</sub>'', ''G<sub>b</sub>P<sub>b</sub>'' and ''G<sub>c</sub>P<sub>c</sub>''.
Then the triangle ''A'B'C'&nbsp;'' is [[Congruence (geometry)|congruent]] to triangle ''ABC'' and its sides are parallel to the sides of triangle ''ABC''.

When ''P'' coincides with the [[orthocenter]] ''H'' of triangle ''ABC'' then the line ''PG'' coincides with the [[Euler line]] of triangle ''ABC''. The triangle ''A'B'C'&nbsp;'' coincides with the Gossard triangle ''A<sub>g</sub>B<sub>g</sub>C<sub>g</sub>'' of triangle ''ABC''.

===Dao's Generalisation ===

The theorem was further generalized by [[Dao Thanh Oai]]. Let ''ABC'' be a triangle. Let ''H'' and ''O'' be two points in the plane, and let the line ''HO'' meets ''BC, CA, AB'' at ''A<sub>0</sub>, B<sub>0</sub>, C<sub>0</sub>'' respectively. Let ''A<sub>H</sub> and A<sub>O</sub>'' be two points such that ''C<sub>0</sub>A<sub>H</sub>'' [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''BH'', ''B<sub>0</sub>A<sub>H</sub>'' [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''CH'' and ''C<sub>0</sub>A<sub>O</sub>'' [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''BO'', ''B<sub>0</sub>A<sub>O</sub>'' [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to ''CO''. Define ''B<sub>H</sub>, B<sub>O</sub>, C<sub>H</sub>, C<sub>O</sub>'' cyclically. Then the triangle formed by the lines ''A<sub>H</sub>A<sub>O</sub>, B<sub>H</sub>B<sub>O</sub>, C<sub>H</sub>C<sub>O</sub>'' and triangle ''ABC'' are homothetic and [[Congruence (geometry)|congruent]], and the [[homothetic center]] lies on the line ''OH''. Dao Thanh Oai's result is generalization of all results above.<ref name=O.T.Dao>[http://www.journal-1.eu/2016-1/Dao-Thanh-Oai-Zeeman-Gossard-pp.76-79.pdf Dao Thanh Oai, ''A generalization of the Zeeman-Gossard perspector theorem'', International Journal of Computer Discovered Mathematics, Vol.1, (2016), Issue 3, page 76-79], {{ISSN|2367-7775}}</ref><ref name=Lozada>[https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETCPart32.html#X63787 César Eliud Lozada, Preamble before  X(63787)][[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]]</ref><ref name=vladimir.shelomovskii>[https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Gossard_perspector Vladimir Shelomovskii, Gossard perspector] [[Art of Problem Solving]]</ref>

* When ''HO'' is the [[Euler line]], Dao's result is the Gossard perspector theorem.
* When ''PQ'' [[Parallel (geometry)|parallel]] to the [[Euler line]], Dao's result is the Zeeman's generalization.
* When ''P'' is the [[centroid]], Dao's result is the Yiu's generalization.
 
The homothetic center in [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]] named '''Dao-Zeeman perspector''' of the line ''OH''.<ref name=Lozada />
